title.narrative: Modernizing Uzbekistan National Innovation System Project

description.narrative: The PDO is to enable the development of a market-oriented National Innovation System in Uzbekistan.

The objective of the Modernizing Uzbekistan National Innovation System (MUNIS) Project for Uzbekistan is to enable the development of a market-oriented National Innovation System. The project has four components. (1) Improving research excellence and commercialization component will improve the capacity of public research to achieve international standards of research quality and enable the commercialization of research results. (2) Promoting innovation in the private sector component will increase private sector innovation in Uzbekistan. It comprises two subcomponents reflecting the dual needs of Uzbekistan at the current stage of development, namely enabling technology adoption by firms and diffusion and supporting the initial growth of R&D-driven innovation, as well as the expansion of a knowledge-based startup sector in Uzbekistan. (3) Supporting STI policy-making and reforms component will address the lack of adequate information about good policies and the weak capacity of policy-making organizations. Importantly, in addition to the support of enabling reforms for project activities, it will also support coordination and consensus building for the implementation of reforms aiming at the development and implementation of new Science Technology and Innovation Strategy of Uzbekistan. The component will finance (i) advisory work for the preparation of studies or draft regulations and policies; (ii) training (e.g., mini-courses) and study tours; and, (iii) consensus-building workshops. MID will encourage women's participation in these events. (4) Project management, and monitoring and evaluation component will support project implementation activities. It will finance the operational costs of the PMU and other related operational costs, including those incurred in the administration of the programs. The PMU will be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of project activities, and for fiduciary activities (including procurement, financial management, environmental and social compliance, reporting citizen engagement, project audits, and other functions).

title.narrative: SMEs that introduced a new product/service

comment.narrative: Number of firms that introduced (a) products or services that are new to the market and (b) products or services that have significant improvements in capabilities, user friendliness, components or sub-systems. Significant improvements include new or significantly improved capabilities or other functions; technical specifications; components and materials; incorporated software; user friendliness. This does not include: i) minor changes; ii) regular seasonal changes; iii) routine upgrades, iv) purely aesthetic design changes that do not affect functionality; v) the resale of a good purchased from other enterprises. Gradual achievement of this indicator will start with the launch of BIRD and ICP programs. A contract with a consulting firm which will implement both programs was signed in spring 2023.

title.narrative: Satisfaction rate of grant applicants on the application process (reflecting transparency and meritocracy)

comment.narrative:
The PMU is responsible for administering an online survey after each call for proposals for the grants programs, aimed at the targeted beneficiaries (including those who had successful applications, rejected applications, or who did not apply) to receive feedback on their perceptions of the meritocracy and transparency of the process. The feedback is reviewed by the grant administrating body to improve the subsequent calls for proposals. The PMU already has M&E specialist and the social specialist to follow the procedure. Collecting the feedback is tied to the first activity - the REP. The PIU has developed a questionnaire, reviewed by the Bank team, and launched the feedback collection among all the REP participants. The questions included, inter alia, the following: "Was there discrimination (based on gender, nationality, education, etc) in the selection of the winners of the contest" and "Are you satisfied with the objectivity of the work of the selection committee".  According to the results of the feedback collection, there were 98 respondents, which participated and were then rejected in the REP 1 andEP2 rounds. Survey results show current 100% satisfaction rate with the application process. 
Feedback will be collected following other grant programs implementation and results will be updated.

Collecting the feedback is tied to the first activity - the REP. The PIU has developed a questionnaire, reviewed by the Bank team,and launchedthe feedback collection among all the REP participants. The questions included, inter alia, the following: Was there discrimination (based on gender, nationality, education, etc) in the selection of the winners of the contest; and Are you satisfied with the objectivity of the work of the selection committee;According to the results of the feedback collection, there were 98respondents, which participated and were then rejected in the REP 1 andEP2 rounds. Survey results show current 100% satisfaction rate with the application process.Feedback will be collected following other grant programs implementation and results will be updated.

title.narrative: Grievance mechanism for all grants programs is established and implemented

comment.narrative: A grievance redress mechanism will be established for each grant program to allow for appeals, complaints and feedback and ensure that the programs remain transparent, meritocratic and responsive to their targeted beneficiaries. The PIU is already equipped with staff to maintain the GRM. The launch of the mechanism came together with the launch of the first project activity, the REP. As of the ISR date no complaints or feedback from the REP or other project participants had been registered.
